hunt.justification: ScreenConnect is a high-trust administrative tool; unauthorized clients provide persistent, unmonitored access that bypasses firewall and identity perimeters. Verifying the integrity of the support infrastructure is critical for MSP-managed estates.

scenario.summary: Threat actors abuse vulnerabilities in ScreenConnect server extensions or hijacked management consoles to deploy unauthorized remote-access clients and the SCKit malware toolkit. The campaign establishes long-term persistence on customer endpoints to host RelayTrap, a component that targets IT technicians' workstations with malicious payloads during support sessions.

meta.rationale: Start with endpoints identified in the scoping query as having ScreenConnect or ConnectWise software. Focus initial behavioral analysis on hosts showing curl activity or silent msiexec parameters.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has abused ScreenConnect management consoles or extension vulnerabilities to silently deploy unauthorized remote-access clients and the SCKit loader toolkit to managed endpoints.

blind_spots.risk: Intruders targeting hosts without an agent will leave no traces in this hunt, creating a blind beachhead.
blind_spots.question: Are unauthorized clients installed on unmanaged endpoints?
blind_spots.remediation: Audit agent coverage against network-discovered ScreenConnect clients.

blind_spots.risk: Without block-level logging, the hunt identifies the loader but not the actual commands SCKit ran after decryption.
blind_spots.question: What did the decoded SCKit scripts execute in memory?
blind_spots.requires: hb_script_activity with full PowerShell Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104)
blind_spots.remediation: Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging via GPO for all managed endpoints.

hunt.name: Unauthorized ScreenConnect Client Deployment
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the initial entry and deployment phase of the SCKit campaign. It first scopes the estate for hosts with ScreenConnect software, then focuses on a lead query identifying silent installations (sc.msi) with session markers (c=Exploited) common in reported attacks. The hunt follows a gated flow: it only performs expensive PowerShell script analysis and fleet-wide command-line prevalence counting if the initial MSI lead is suspicious. This ensures high-fidelity triage of unauthorized support software without manual review of every legitimate installation.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%screenconnect%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%connectwise%')
config.description: Find the hosts that currently have ScreenConnect or ConnectWise software to narrow the hunt scope.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts with ScreenConnect installed. Presence of the software is expected; silence means the software is not inventoried or is missing from the estate.

nodes.label: Lead: Silent MSI deployment with exploited markers

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%sc.msi%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%c=exploited%') AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%msiexec%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%curl%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify suspicious MSI installations involving sc.msi or session markers like c=Exploited initiated via curl or msiexec.
config.expected_signal: Command lines showing curl downloading sc.msi or msiexec installing it silently. The presence of session markers in the URL is a high-confidence lead.

config.objective: Determine if the command lines in lead-unauthorized-msi-install match the research for SCKit deployment, specifically focusing on unauthorized download sources or c=Exploited markers.
config.description: Decide whether the observed lead represents a targeted intrusion attempt requiring further evidence collection.
config.expected_signal: A suspicious or benign verdict for each host based on the MSI command line structure.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of suspicious or benign, citing specific command strings.

config.question: the evaluate-lead verdict is suspicious for at least one host
config.condition: the evaluate-lead verdict is suspicious for at least one host
config.description: Terminate the hunt if no suspicious installations are found, saving resources for the more expensive script analysis.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, script_name, script_content, time FROM hb_script_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{sckit_scripts}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(script_name) || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%panel-lateral%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%relaytrap%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify the execution of the PowerShell-based decoders and loaders that extract the SCKit toolkit.
config.expected_signal: Script blocks matching the toolkit logic. Finding these on the same hosts as the MSI lead strongly corroborates a compromise.

primitive_config.expected: Script blocks matching the toolkit logic. Finding these on the same hosts as the MSI lead strongly corroborates a compromise.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_cmd_line) AS cmd, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%sc.msi%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%c=exploited%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1 HAVING hosts <= 3
config.description: Stack-count the installation commands to separate legitimate fleet-wide management activity from unique, attacker-controlled outliers.
config.expected_signal: Command lines seen on only one or two hosts. Genuine MSP maintenance will typically have high host counts.

primitive_config.label: Prevalence of MSI installation commands
primitive_config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_cmd_line) AS cmd, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%sc.msi%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%c=exploited%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1 HAVING hosts <= 3
primitive_config.expected: Command lines seen on only one or two hosts. Genuine MSP maintenance will typically have high host counts.

config.objective: Determine if the host was targeted by SCKit by weighing the rarity of its MSI installation command line against the presence of known toolkit PowerShell script blocks.
config.description: Correlate the behavioral lead, PowerShell script content, and fleet-wide prevalence to reach a final verdict per host.
config.expected_signal: A high-confidence verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign for every host showing evidence of ScreenConnect client deployment.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict citing specific rows from process and script surfaces.

config.question: the triage-deployment verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the triage-deployment verdict is malicious for at least one host

config.description: Verify the findings, identify the management server used to issue the commands, and audit for persistence.
config.instructions: Review the triage evidence. Identify the origin of the management commands (e.g., vulnerable RMM+ extension). Audit the registry and scheduled tasks for follow-on SCKit persistence components.

config.description: Record findings and findings to improve standing detections.
